seoTitle: Post-Study Work Options: UK Graduate Visa, US OPT and Other Routes
title: Post-Study Work Options: UK Graduate Visa, US OPT and Other Routes
content:
Post-study work permission depends on the country, qualification and immigration rules. Compare what each route allows, when you must apply and what comes after it; do not treat temporary permission as permanent residence.

Compare permissions rather than informal names

'Post-study work' describes an intention, not one international visa category. The UK Graduate route, Canada's post-graduation work permit, Australia's Temporary Graduate visa and US Optional Practical Training have different eligibility rules and application processes. Avoid treating 'PSW' as an official name that means the same thing everywhere.

UK: the Graduate route

The UK route is available only after an eligible course and when the other application conditions are met. Under current guidance, non-doctoral applications made on or after 1 January 2027 receive 18 months, while doctoral qualifications have a three-year period. Check the application date and your qualification before planning around a duration.

The route does not guarantee a sponsored job or permanent residence. An applicant may need a different immigration route when the permission ends. Scholarship return-home conditions can also affect the plan.

United States: Optional Practical Training

OPT is connected to F-1 student status and practical training relevant to the degree. It involves eligibility, recommendations or authorisation and timing requirements. Ask the institution's designated school official to explain the process before accepting work or making travel arrangements.

An extension for a qualifying STEM degree has additional conditions. Do not assume that any technical course or research role qualifies, or that OPT guarantees a later employment visa.

Canada and Australia

Check whether the institution, programme, qualification and your individual circumstances satisfy the current requirements for the Canadian or Australian route. Rules can differ by degree and application circumstances. Use the government pages and the institution's international student advisers instead of relying on an older generic duration table.

Make a decision checklist

Record the eligible qualification, application window, work conditions, expected costs and the next possible immigration route. Also consider the labour market for your actual occupation and whether employers offer roles suitable for your experience. Temporary work permission is useful only when it fits a realistic plan for employment and finances.

Recheck the official rules close to graduation. Requirements in force when you begin a degree may not be the requirements that apply when you finish.

Official information

  • UK Graduate visa
  • USCIS: OPT for F-1 students
  • Canada: work after graduation
  • Australia: Temporary Graduate visa

Plan around eligibility, not the route name

For each country, record the qualification and institution requirements, application timing, permitted work and any conditions on renewal or switching status. Keep a note of the official page and the date you checked it. If your degree or funding award has additional conditions, include those in the comparison. The purpose is to understand which options could apply to you after graduation, not to select a route from a headline. Avoid building your finances around future employment that you have not secured or immigration permission that has not been granted.

Relevant listings and guides on NextApply

To see how these questions apply to a real listing, review Cancer Research UK Manchester Institute Four-Year PhD Studentships 2027. Compare its stated requirements with your own preparation and check the official source before applying.

You can also browse University of Manchester on NextApply and the PhD positions category. Listings and recruitment windows can change.
